# Google Workspace Ops

Curated by Skill Harbor: a workflow skill for operating Google Workspace assets as working systems rather than editing files in isolation. It treats Drive as the entry point, then routes to the right specialist: Docs for text-heavy documents, Sheets for tabular work with formulas and charts, Slides for decks, imports, and template migration. The method is inspect-first: locate the exact file plus siblings and likely duplicates through Drive search (confirming by title, owner, or modified time when several look alike), summarize the current structure (tabs, headings, slide count), then edit with precision (index-aware edits in Docs, explicit tabs and ranges in Sheets, content edits distinguished from visual cleanup in Slides). It also keeps the whole system clean over time, surfacing duplicate trackers, stale decks, and outdated docs, and recommending archive, merge, or rename. Output follows a fixed ASSET / CURRENT STATE / ACTION / FOLLOW-UPS format, which makes every intervention reviewable. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: pure guidance, nothing to install; the agent needs access to your Google Workspace (Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides) to act, otherwise it can only plan the work for you. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
